scenario: 面试官问「Tell me about a conflict with a coworker.」你想开头，却先 echo 问题、再绕进背景不落点。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks, "Tell me about a conflict with a coworker." You want to open, but you echo the question and drift into background without landing.
q: 该怎么用一句话开这个冲突——一句背景 + 利害？
q_en: How do you open the conflict in one line — the situation plus what was at stake?
options: So, so there was one time — a coworker, we had, I mean it wasn't really a conflict, but we we didn't agree on the API thing, so yeah, at that time...
We had a disagreement over the API design, and the team talked it through, and eventually we reached an agreement together in the end.
A backend engineer and I disagreed on the campaign API contract right before a launch — if we didn't settle it, the release would slip.
I shall recount an interpersonal disagreement pertaining to divergent architectural viewpoints on the API contract layer.
options_en: So, so there was one time — a coworker, we had, I mean it wasn't really a conflict, but we we didn't agree on the API thing, so yeah, at that time...
We had a disagreement over the API design, and the team talked it through, and eventually we reached an agreement together in the end.
A backend engineer and I disagreed on the campaign API contract right before a launch — if we didn't settle it, the release would slip.
I shall recount an interpersonal disagreement pertaining to divergent architectural viewpoints on the API contract layer.
tradeoff: 一句给冲突双方+利害 vs 绕起步：先 echo 问题、再 so/we 拖着，代价是听半天不知道冲突是什么。
why: Situation 一句就落地：谁跟谁、为什么、利害是什么。别像原话 echo 问题再用 so/we 绕，句子还没起就散了。
why_en: Land the Situation in one line — who, over what, and what was at stake — instead of echoing the question and stalling on "so, we."
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官只要个一句话标题、马上要追问细节，那「I had a disagreement with a teammate」这种更短的点名也够。
optionMeanings: 拖着 so/we 起步，绕半天没点出冲突。
全用 we、没有利害，像集体协商。
一句给出冲突双方 + 利害。
「shall recount pertaining」式书面腔。
optionMeanings_en: Stalls on "so, we" — never names the conflict.
All "we," no stakes — sounds like a group chat.
One line: who, over what, what was at stake.
A "shall recount pertaining" written register.
optionScenarioImpacts: 面试官等半天不知道冲突到底是什么。
听不出你的立场，你像个旁观者。
一句话对方就抓住冲突和利害。
念文档腔，没有真实的冲突感。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They wait and still don't know the conflict.
No stance — you sound like a bystander.
One line and they grab the conflict and stakes.
Doc register — no real sense of conflict.
optionDirectness: 几乎没有合适的场合。
只有真是纯集体决策时才勉强。
正好接住「讲一次冲突」。
只适合写在纠纷记录里，不适合开口。
optionDirectness_en: Almost no situation fits this.
Barely fits if it truly was a group call.
Hits "tell me about a conflict" exactly.
Fits a dispute log, not speech.

termDefinitions.meaning: 调用方和服务方约定好的接口形状——字段、类型、返回值，改它会牵动两边。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API contract is the agreed shape of an interface — its fields, types, and responses — that both caller and service depend on.

scenario: 冲突讲到「你怎么处理的」，你习惯用 we 把自己藏起来，面试官听不出你个人做了什么。
scenario_en: The conflict reaches "what did you do," and you slip into "we," hiding yourself — the interviewer can't tell what you personally did.
q: 该怎么说清冲突里「你」具体做了什么（用 I，不是 we）？
q_en: How do you state what YOU did in the conflict — in "I," not "we"?
options: So I set up a quick call, walked him through both designs on a doc, and proposed we split it — my API, his validation rules.
We discussed it as a team, we looked at both sides, and we came to a solution that worked for everyone in the end.
I, so I tried to, we kind of talked, and then, um, I think we, we sort of found a way, I mean eventually, to to move forward...
I facilitated a synchronous alignment session to reconcile the conflicting proposals and drive convergence toward mutual consensus.
options_en: So I set up a quick call, walked him through both designs on a doc, and proposed we split it — my API, his validation rules.
We discussed it as a team, we looked at both sides, and we came to a solution that worked for everyone in the end.
I, so I tried to, we kind of talked, and then, um, I think we, we sort of found a way, I mean eventually, to to move forward...
I facilitated a synchronous alignment session to reconcile the conflicting proposals and drive convergence toward mutual consensus.
tradeoff: 用 I 说清你的动作 vs 躲进 we：全程 we 听着谦虚，代价是面试官不知道到底是你还是别人解决的。
why: Action 这一拍全程用「I」：我约了、我讲了、我提议。别把自己藏进 we，那样面试官看不出这段是你的功劳。
why_en: Own the Action in "I" — I set up, I walked him through, I proposed — don't bury yourself in "we" where your part disappears.
whenOtherWins: 如果这一步确实是集体共识、没有你主导的动作，那如实说 we 反而诚实——但别在你明明主导时也用 we。
optionMeanings: 全程用 I，说清你的三个具体动作。
全用 we，你的动作全被抹平。
I 和 we 混着卡，绕了一圈没说清。
「facilitated synchronous alignment」式书面腔。
optionMeanings_en: All "I" — three concrete actions you took.
All "we" — your actions get flattened away.
Mixes I and we, stalls, never lands.
A "facilitated synchronous alignment" register.
optionScenarioImpacts: 面试官清楚看到是你推动了和解。
听不出你做了什么，功劳归了集体。
绕一圈，对方抓不住你的具体动作。
术语堆砌，像念流程文档不像讲事。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They see clearly that you drove the fix.
Your part vanishes into the group.
Circles once — they can't grab your action.
Jargon pile — sounds like a process doc.
optionDirectness: 正好接住「你具体怎么做的」。
只有真是集体共识时才诚实合适。
几乎没有合适的场合。
只适合写在会议纪要里，不适合开口。
optionDirectness_en: Hits "what did you do" exactly.
Only honest if it truly was a group call.
Almost no situation fits this.
Fits meeting minutes, not speech.

termDefinitions.meaning: 校验规则——挡住非法输入、保证数据合法的那组检查。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Validation rules are the checks that block illegal input and keep data well-formed.

scenario: 面试官问失败「And what did you learn?」你常常没有 result 也没有 learning，草草收尾就停下。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks about a failure, "And what did you learn?" You often have no result and no lesson, and just trail off.
q: 该怎么给这个失败一个 result + 学到什么？
q_en: How do you close the failure with a result plus what you learned?
options: Yeah, so that was the mistake, and after that it was fine, we fixed it, and that's basically the whole story I guess.
So what I learned, I learned that, um, edge cases are, are important, and also to to test more, and, you know, to be more careful next time, I guess, so yeah, that's the main thing...
The incident engendered salient learnings concerning comprehensive edge-case coverage and rigorous pre-merge validation discipline.
About two hundred campaigns saved in a bad state before we caught it. Since then I write the edge-case tests first, before the happy path.
options_en: Yeah, so that was the mistake, and after that it was fine, we fixed it, and that's basically the whole story I guess.
So what I learned, I learned that, um, edge cases are, are important, and also to to test more, and, you know, to be more careful next time, I guess, so yeah, that's the main thing...
The incident engendered salient learnings concerning comprehensive edge-case coverage and rigorous pre-merge validation discipline.
About two hundred campaigns saved in a bad state before we caught it. Since then I write the edge-case tests first, before the happy path.
tradeoff: 数字 result + 具体改变 vs 草草收尾：说「后来就好了」听着轻松，代价是失败没落点、也没学到东西。
why: Result 一拍给两样：一个数字（多大影响）+ 一个具体改变（你现在怎么做了）。别停在「后来就好了」或空泛的「要更小心」。
why_en: Close with two things — a number for the impact and one concrete change you made since — not a vague "it got fixed" or "be more careful."
whenOtherWins: 如果这次失败影响很小、没有值得报的数字，那老实说「影响不大，但我学到…」直接跳到教训也可以。
optionMeanings: 「后来就好了」——没数字也没教训。
卡着说「要更小心」，教训很空。
「engendered salient learnings」式书面腔。
一个数字 result + 一个具体改变。
optionMeanings_en: "It got fixed" — no number, no lesson.
Stalls on "be more careful" — empty lesson.
An "engendered salient learnings" register.
A number result plus one concrete change.
optionScenarioImpacts: 失败没落点，像你没真反思过。
教训太空泛，面试官记不住。
书面腔盖住了你到底改了什么。
数字加改变，成长显得真实可信。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: No landing — sounds like no real reflection.
Lesson too vague — nothing to remember.
Register hides what you actually changed.
Number plus change — the growth feels real.
optionDirectness: 几乎没有合适的场合。
只有对方只想听一句感受时才勉强。
只适合写在事故复盘文档里。
正好接住「你学到了什么」。
optionDirectness_en: Almost no situation fits this.
Barely fits if they want one feeling-line.
Fits a postmortem doc, not speech.
Hits "what did you learn" exactly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在边界或非常规输入下才触发的特殊情况，最容易被漏测。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An edge case is an unusual or boundary input that's easy to miss when testing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一切输入正常、不出错的那条主流程，区别于异常分支。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The happy path is the normal, error-free main flow, as opposed to the error branches.

scenario: 面试官问「Tell me about a time you led something.」你把自己的职责说成团队的，说不清「你负责什么」。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks, "Tell me about a time you led something." You describe your responsibility as the team's, and can't pin down what YOU owned.
q: 该怎么一句说清这次带头「你」具体负责什么（Task 拍）？
q_en: How do you name your specific responsibility in one line — the Task beat?
options: The team was building the Promotion Day feature, and we all worked on different parts of it together over the quarter.
I owned the design for Promotion Day's precedence logic, and I coordinated two other engineers on the rollout.
So my role was, I was kind of, I mean I was leading, but also we, the team, so I was responsible for, for the main part...
I took full charge of the architectural design and cross-functional coordination responsibilities for the Promotion Day initiative.
options_en: The team was building the Promotion Day feature, and we all worked on different parts of it together over the quarter.
I owned the design for Promotion Day's precedence logic, and I coordinated two other engineers on the rollout.
So my role was, I was kind of, I mean I was leading, but also we, the team, so I was responsible for, for the main part...
I took full charge of the architectural design and cross-functional coordination responsibilities for the Promotion Day initiative.
tradeoff: 一句锚定你负责的那块 vs 说成团队的活儿：讲「the team was building」听着谦虚，代价是听不出你带的是什么。
why: Task 一拍说清你个人负责哪一块：我 own 了什么、我协调了谁。别把职责说成「the team was building」，那样你的 leadership 就没了。
why_en: In the Task beat, name your own slice — what you owned and who you coordinated — not "the team was building," which erases your leadership.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官先问「这个项目是什么」，那先一句给团队背景、再落到你负责的部分也合理——顺序跟着问题走。
optionMeanings: 把职责说成团队的，你带了什么看不见。
一句锚定你 own 的那块 + 协调了谁。
I 和 we 混着卡，说不清自己的角色。
「assumed ownership of coordination」式书面腔。
optionMeanings_en: Frames it as the team's — your lead vanishes.
One line: what you owned, who you coordinated.
Stalls between I and we — role stays unclear.
An "assumed ownership of coordination" register.
optionScenarioImpacts: 听不出你带头，像团队里普通一员。
对方一句就懂你负责哪块、带了谁。
绕半天，面试官抓不住你的角色。
书面腔盖住了你实际带的具体工作。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: No lead shows — you're just one of the team.
They instantly see your slice and who you led.
Circles — they can't pin your role.
Register hides the actual work you led.
optionDirectness: 只有对方先要项目背景时才顺。
正好接住「你带头负责什么」。

只适合写在岗位职责说明里。
optionDirectness_en: Fits only if they asked for project context first.
Hits "what did you lead" exactly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多条策略同时适用时，决定哪条优先生效的那部分逻辑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precedence logic decides which rule or strategy wins when several apply at once.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个功能逐步上线、放量给用户的过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rollout is the process of gradually releasing a feature to users.

scenario: 带头的活儿讲到「你怎么推动的」，你又滑回 we，面试官看不出这是你 drive 的。
scenario_en: The leadership story reaches "how did you drive it," and you slip back into "we" — the interviewer can't tell you drove it.
q: 该怎么说清带头时「你」推动了什么（别滑回 we）？
q_en: How do you show what YOU drove as the lead — without slipping into "we"?
options: So then I, we sort of, I pushed for, I mean the team, we we decided to, and then I kind of drove the, the timeline thing, I don't know, eventually it, it got done...
We aligned on a plan, we split up the work, and we kept each other updated until it shipped on time.
I wrote the rollout plan, ran a daily fifteen-minute sync, and unblocked the two engineers when they hit a schema question.
I orchestrated the execution plan and instituted a daily synchronization cadence to systematically mitigate blockers.
options_en: So then I, we sort of, I pushed for, I mean the team, we we decided to, and then I kind of drove the, the timeline thing, I don't know, eventually it, it got done...
We aligned on a plan, we split up the work, and we kept each other updated until it shipped on time.
I wrote the rollout plan, ran a daily fifteen-minute sync, and unblocked the two engineers when they hit a schema question.
I orchestrated the execution plan and instituted a daily synchronization cadence to systematically mitigate blockers.
tradeoff: 用 I 给三个 drive 动作 vs 躲进 we：全程 we 听着不抢功，代价是 leadership 全被抹平。
why: 带头的 Action 用「I」给具体动词：我写了计划、我开了同步、我解了阻塞。原话在 I/we 之间反复横跳，drive 感就没了。
why_en: Drive the Action in "I" with concrete verbs — I wrote, I ran, I unblocked — not the I/we flip-flop that erases the sense you led.
whenOtherWins: 如果对方在意的是团队协作氛围而非你个人主导，那多用 we 强调 collaboration 也读得通——看问题重点。
optionMeanings: 在 I 和 we 里来回蹦，你的主导全糊掉。
全用 we，你的推动被抹成集体行动。
用 I 给三个具体的 drive 动作。
「orchestrated instituted cadence」式书面腔。
optionMeanings_en: Flip-flops I/we — the sense you drove it dies.
All "we" — your driving flattens to group work.
Three concrete driving verbs in "I."
An "orchestrated instituted cadence" register.

听着像大家一起漂，没有掌舵的人。
对方清楚看到你在具体地推动。
术语盖住动作，像念项目管理模板。

Sounds like everyone drifting, no one steering.
They see you concretely driving it.

只有对方在意协作氛围时才勉强。

Barely fits if they care about collaboration vibe.

termDefinitions.meaning: 帮别人清除挡住进度的障碍，让他能继续往下做。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To unblock someone is to clear whatever is stopping them so they can keep moving.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据的结构定义——表、字段、类型和它们之间的关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A schema is the defined structure of data — its tables, fields, types, and relationships.

scenario: 面试官问「Tell me about a hard decision you made.」你铺垫太久、echo 问题，一直到不了那个决定。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks, "Tell me about a hard decision you made." You over-build the setup and echo the question, never reaching the decision.
q: 该怎么一句把这个艰难决定的背景 + 利害说清（Situation 拍）？
q_en: How do you land the hard decision's situation and stakes in one line?
options: Two weeks before launch I had to choose: ship Promotion Day on the old schema, or delay to redesign it clean.
So a hard decision, hmm, so there was, when we were, so at that time we had to, to decide whether to, to kind of...
The team faced a tough call about whether to ship on the existing schema or take more time, and it was a big decision for us.
I was confronted with a consequential decision regarding schema-migration timing relative to the impending launch deadline.
options_en: Two weeks before launch I had to choose: ship Promotion Day on the old schema, or delay to redesign it clean.
So a hard decision, hmm, so there was, when we were, so at that time we had to, to decide whether to, to kind of...
The team faced a tough call about whether to ship on the existing schema or take more time, and it was a big decision for us.
I was confronted with a consequential decision regarding schema-migration timing relative to the impending launch deadline.
tradeoff: 一句给决定的两个选项 + 时间压力 vs 铺垫绕圈：echo「a hard decision」再拖，代价是决定始终没端出来。
why: Situation 一句给出两难：时间压力 + 摆在你面前的两个选项。原话 echo 问题再绕，一直到不了决定本身。
why_en: State the dilemma in one line — the time pressure and the two options in front of you — instead of echoing "a hard decision" and circling.
whenOtherWins: 如果背景很复杂、一句说不清，那先花一两句交代约束、再端出决定也可以——但别停在 echo 问题上空转。
optionMeanings: 一句给出时间压力 + 两个选项。
echo 问题再拖，决定始终没端出来。
说成团队的决定，你的判断被隐去。
「confronted with a consequential」式书面腔。
optionMeanings_en: One line: time pressure plus the two options.
Echoes the question, stalls, never lands it.
Frames it as the team's — your call disappears.
A "confronted with a consequential" register.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方一句就懂你两难在哪。
绕半天，面试官等不到那个决定。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据的结构从旧定义改成新定义的过程，改动风险高、要小心迁移。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A schema migration is changing the structure of stored data from an old definition to a new one — risky, and done carefully.

scenario: 艰难决定讲到结果，你要么把数字埋掉、要么干脆只说「it worked out okay」没有 result。
scenario_en: The hard-decision story reaches the result, and you either bury the number or just say "it worked out okay" with no real result.
q: 该怎么给这个决定一个带数字的 result（Result 拍）？
q_en: How do you close the decision with a result that carries a number?
options: So in the end it worked out okay, the launch happened, and I think everyone was pretty happy with how it went overall.
I shipped on the old schema and paid it back later — we hit the launch date, and Promotion Day drove about fifteen percent more spend.
The result was, um, it was good, we we launched, and the number went up by, by some amount, like fifteen or so percent maybe, I don't remember the exact figure honestly...
The decision culminated in on-time delivery and yielded an approximate fifteen-percent uplift in advertiser spend metrics.
options_en: So in the end it worked out okay, the launch happened, and I think everyone was pretty happy with how it went overall.
I shipped on the old schema and paid it back later — we hit the launch date, and Promotion Day drove about fifteen percent more spend.
The result was, um, it was good, we we launched, and the number went up by, by some amount, like fifteen or so percent maybe, I don't remember the exact figure honestly...
The decision culminated in on-time delivery and yielded an approximate fifteen-percent uplift in advertiser spend metrics.
tradeoff: 决定 + 数字结果 vs 「worked out okay」：说「大家挺满意」听着舒服，代价是结果没重量、记不住。
why: Result 把你的决定接到一个数字上：赶上了 deadline，带来约 15% 增量。别停在『挺好的』这种软话，也别把数字说得含糊。
why_en: Tie your decision to a number — we hit the date and it drove about fifteen percent more spend — not a soft "it worked out okay."
whenOtherWins: 如果结果不方便透露具体数字，那用相对量级「主要指标明显上升」也行——关键是别停在「挺好的」这种没重量的话。
optionMeanings: 「worked out okay」——没有数字的软收尾。
决定 + 一个具体的数字结果。
卡着把数字说得含糊，结果没落实。
「culminated yielded uplift」式书面腔。
optionMeanings_en: "Worked out okay" — a soft, numberless close.
The decision plus one concrete number.
Stalls and blurs the number — result never lands.
A "culminated yielded uplift" register.

数字一出，你的决定立刻可信。
数字含糊，像临场编的不可信。
书面腔像念财报，不像讲你的成果。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: No weight — they forget it right after.
The number makes your decision credible.

Fits a quarterly report, not speech.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先用有欠缺的方案上线，之后再补上本该做的清理或重构，即偿还技术债。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To pay it back is to ship a shortcut now and do the proper cleanup or rework later — repaying technical debt.

termDefinitions.meaning: 广告主投放广告实际花掉的钱，是衡量广告产品成效的核心指标之一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Spend is the money advertisers actually put into running ads — a core metric for an ads product's success.

scenario: 面试官问「Tell me about a failure.」你讲成一团，全是背景没有动作、也没有结果，四拍全糊在一起。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks, "Tell me about a failure." It comes out as a blur — all context, no action, no result — the four beats mashed together.
q: 该怎么用四拍（背景→我的责任→我做了什么→结果/教训）讲完这个失败？
q_en: How do you walk the failure in four beats — situation, your part, what you did, result and lesson?
options: So there was this failure, and, so basically what happened was, we we had a bug, and then, um, it was kind of my, our fault, and then it got, it got fixed I think...
We were migrating the budget service — big project, lots of moving parts, tight deadline, many teams involved, a really complex quarter for everyone.
I shall enumerate a failure scenario encompassing situation, responsibility, remediation, and the resultant learnings derived therefrom.
I pushed a config change with no flag, it broke budget writes for twenty minutes, I rolled it back, and now I always gate configs behind a flag.
options_en: So there was this failure, and, so basically what happened was, we we had a bug, and then, um, it was kind of my, our fault, and then it got, it got fixed I think...
We were migrating the budget service — big project, lots of moving parts, tight deadline, many teams involved, a really complex quarter for everyone.
I shall enumerate a failure scenario encompassing situation, responsibility, remediation, and the resultant learnings derived therefrom.
I pushed a config change with no flag, it broke budget writes for twenty minutes, I rolled it back, and now I always gate configs behind a flag.
tradeoff: 四拍各一句、干净走完 vs 全是背景：铺一堆 context 听着在认真交代，代价是动作和结果一个都没到。
why: 失败走紧凑四拍：我做了什么错事、造成什么影响、我怎么补救、之后怎么改。原话全是 context 没动作，第二个选项也只堆背景。
why_en: Walk the failure in four tight beats — what I did wrong, the impact, how I fixed it, what I changed since — not a blur of context with no action.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官明确说「先给我背景」，那先展开 Situation 再讲后面三拍也行——但别让整段都停在背景上。
optionMeanings: 四拍糊成一团，动作和结果都没到。
全是背景铺陈，没有动作也没有结果。
「shall enumerate encompassing」式书面腔。
四拍各一句，干净走完整段失败。
optionMeanings_en: Four beats mashed — no action, no result reached.
All context piled up — no action, no result.
A "shall enumerate encompassing" register.
Four beats, one line each, walked clean.
optionScenarioImpacts: 一团糊，面试官抓不到任何一拍。
堆完背景就没了，像没讲到失败本身。
念结构名词，听不出真发生了什么。
四拍清晰，对方一遍就懂整个失败。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: A blur — they can't grab a single beat.
Context ends and stops — the failure never arrives.
Naming the beats, not living them — no real story.
Four clean beats — they get the whole failure once.
optionDirectness: 几乎没有合适的场合。
只有对方明确要你先给背景时才勉强。
只适合写在复盘模板标题里。
正好接住「讲一次失败」。
optionDirectness_en: Almost no situation fits this.
Barely fits if they explicitly asked for context first.
Fits a postmortem template heading, not speech.
Hits "tell me about a failure" exactly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个开关，让新代码先关着上线、再按需打开，出问题能立刻关掉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feature flag is a switch that ships new code turned off, so it can be enabled gradually and killed instantly if it breaks.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把线上改动撤回到上一个正常版本，即「回滚」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To roll back is to revert a live change to the last working version.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把广告预算的改动写入系统的操作；写失败意味着预算无法更新。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Budget writes are the operations that save changes to ad budgets; if they fail, budgets can't update.
